## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | CONFIRMED |
| Confidence | HIGH |
| Severity | MEDIUM |
| Task Type | Bug fix with regression coverage |

### What Was Claimed

Issue #92 reports that picked-up issues advance through durable workflow phases while their visible `workflow:*` label remains stale. The expected projection is one canonical workflow label for the current phase, with unrelated labels preserved.

### What We Found

`GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel` already performs the correct replacement primitive: it reads the issue, removes labels beginning with `workflow:` (and the projection-owned `needs-human` label), preserves all other labels, and writes the new canonical label. Its adapter test verifies replacement and preservation.

The defect is in lifecycle coverage. The child checkpoint projection maps only investigation/build/review starts and investigation completion. It does not project every phase boundary, including direct/legacy transition into `workflow:awaiting-merge` before merge and the terminal `workflow:merged` transition. The legacy finalizer appends merge, close, and cleanup phase events without projecting a stage at their boundaries. The node-oriented path has a separate mapping, so the same durable lifecycle can take different label paths depending on execution mode.

### Root Cause

Workflow labels are emitted opportunistically by multiple execution paths instead of being derived and projected consistently from every durable phase/node transition. In particular, direct finalization can record a successful review and start merge while leaving the issue at `workflow:in-review`; completion-only checkpoints for build/review stages also do not repair a stale label. Durable state can therefore advance without a matching visible projection.

### Affected Files

| Path | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` | Checkpoint-to-label mapping for direct/bounded child execution |
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Node and legacy lifecycle projection, including merge/close/cleanup |
| `src/adapters/github-projection.ts` | Canonical replacement primitive to retain and exercise |
| `test/agents/child-runtime-commit.test.ts` or a focused child-runtime test | Regression coverage for checkpoint mappings |
| `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` | Regression coverage for node/direct lifecycle mappings |

### Evidence

- `workflowLabelForCheckpoint` returns labels for selected `start` actions and only `investigate` on `complete`.
- `#finalize` calls `appendPhase(..., "merge", "start", ...)` but does not project `awaitingMerge` before the merge effect.
- `#finalize` projects `merged` only after merge completion, so a stale pre-merge label can persist throughout the awaiting-merge window.
- `setWorkflowLabel` filters every prior `workflow:*` label and preserves labels such as `bug` and `priority:P1`.
- Existing tests verify the primitive and isolated stage mapping, but no test drives all canonical lifecycle labels through both paths.

### History Findings

The checked-out frozen base already contains partial workflow-label support and tests for label replacement. The remaining inconsistency is structural: checkpoint and node/legacy finalization paths use different transition maps. No repository guidance authorizes a domain-specific bypass or label mutation outside the projector.

### Recommendation

Centralize the canonical phase-to-label mapping used by checkpoint and node/legacy transitions, invoke it on every relevant start/completion boundary (including `awaiting-merge` and `merged`), and add deterministic tests that assert replacement of stale workflow labels while preserving unrelated labels across the lifecycle. Keep projection failure non-authoritative: durable state remains authoritative and reconciliation must retry the same projection.

### Related Issues

- Issue #92 (current): workflow labels do not update as picked-up issues change phase.
- No additional related issue was identified in the checked-out repository.

### Decomposition Assessment

The fix is bounded to workflow projection mapping, call sites, and regression tests. It does not require decomposition, a product decision, UX redesign, policy change, or protected-branch/security authority.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Investigation, ready-to-build, building, in-review, awaiting-merge, and merged transitions each project their canonical label.
- [ ] Every transition removes the previous `workflow:*` label.
- [ ] Unrelated labels remain unchanged.
- [ ] Direct/bounded and node/parent lifecycle paths share equivalent label behavior.
- [ ] Automated tests cover the complete lifecycle and stale-label repair.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

## Builder Contract

### Scope

Implement deterministic workflow-label projection for every supported lifecycle boundary in the issue #92 work-on paths. Reuse the existing `GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel` replacement semantics; do not alter GitHub authentication, state authority, merge policy, or label ownership rules.

### Allowed Files

| Path | Allowed Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts` | Add one shared phase-to-canonical-label mapping helper if needed by both runtimes. |
| `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` | Use the shared mapping for checkpoint start/completion projection and expose only focused pure behavior needed by tests. |
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Project awaiting-merge at legacy merge start and preserve/repair merged-stage projection at terminal parent boundaries; keep node-stage mapping consistent. |
| `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts` | Extend replacement/preservation coverage across the canonical lifecycle. |
| `test/agents/child-runtime-commit.test.ts` | Cover checkpoint-to-label mappings, including merge and terminal phases. |
| `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` | Cover node transition mappings and terminal-stage repair behavior. |

No other files may be modified.

### Behavioral Invariants

- Exactly one current `workflow:*` label is retained after a successful projection.
- Non-workflow issue labels remain unchanged.
- Canonical labels are `workflow:investigating`, `workflow:ready-to-build`, `workflow:building`, `workflow:in-review`, `workflow:awaiting-merge`, and `workflow:merged` (with existing invalid/decomposed terminal labels retained).
- Durable journal state remains authoritative; projection errors continue to be retried/reconciled and never become a successful state transition.
- Direct/bounded checkpoint execution and node/parent execution produce the same label for equivalent phase boundaries.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Investigation start and completion project investigating or ready-to-build, including invalid/decomposed outcomes.
- [ ] Plan, worktree, implementation, and verification start/completion project building.
- [ ] Review and preparation boundaries project in-review.
- [ ] Merge start projects awaiting-merge and merge completion projects merged.
- [ ] Close/cleanup terminal boundaries preserve or repair merged, while invalid/decomposed paths retain their terminal labels.
- [ ] Previous workflow labels are removed and unrelated labels are preserved.
- [ ] Automated tests cover the lifecycle and stale-label replacement.

### Verification

Run only the tracked `check` command through `forge_verify`. GitHub CI remains parent-owned after PR preparation.
<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

The projector already reads issue labels and performs a replace-style `PUT` that filters prior `workflow:*` labels and the projection-owned `needs-human` label while retaining unrelated labels. The missing behavior is lifecycle coverage: `workflowLabelForCheckpoint` currently handles only selected starts and investigation completion, while legacy finalization records merge/close/cleanup phase events without projecting their stages. The node path has a separate mapping and does not repair a merged label at ordinary close/cleanup boundaries.

The shared mapping will accept a run phase, transition (`start` or `complete`), and optional investigation report. It will return the canonical label for every phase boundary without performing side effects. The existing node mapping remains outcome-aware for review decisions and merge outcomes; its terminal close/cleanup fallback will return merged only for normal post-merge completion.

Projection calls will remain after durable events are written. A failed projection will retain existing retry/reconciliation behavior, and tests will use deterministic transports/pure functions rather than network access or production artifacts.
<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->
<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Add a shared phase checkpoint label resolver beside `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE`, covering start/completion for resolve, investigate, build phases, review, merge, close, and cleanup; recognize invalid/decomposed investigation reports without inferring unrelated outcomes.
2. Replace the child-runtime’s partial local resolver with the shared resolver and export the pure resolver only as a testable deterministic projection seam.
3. Update legacy finalization to project `workflow:awaiting-merge` immediately after the durable merge start boundary, and project the merged stage at close/cleanup boundaries where needed for repair.
4. Update node transition mapping so ordinary close/cleanup completion resolves to merged while preserving invalid/decomposed terminal outcomes.
5. Extend adapter, child-runtime, and work-on tests to assert all canonical labels, stale workflow replacement, unrelated-label preservation, and equivalent node/checkpoint mappings.
6. Run the bound `check` verification command, inspect the resulting diff, and commit only the approved files.

### Risks And Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Label projection fails after a durable event | Keep existing warning/reconciliation behavior; no state rollback or false success. |
| Terminal invalid/decomposed issue is relabeled merged | Check investigation outcome/report before normal terminal fallback. |
| Duplicate labels or unrelated labels are lost | Reuse `setWorkflowLabel` and assert exact sets in adapter tests. |
| Direct and node paths diverge again | Shared phase resolver plus explicit node lifecycle assertions. |
